title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Lessons from Biological World Models for Testing Action Effects
summary: In v2, frozen diffusion-model predictions exposed pooling tests that missed known actions in 96/96 segments while the registered alternative detected them.
ai_technology: Frozen pretrained DIAMOND models supplied frame predictions for the statistical tests
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Frozen pretrained DIAMOND models supplied frame predictions for the statistical tests; their predictions were not treated as measured biological outcomes.; Version 2 reports the pooled statistic detecting 0/96 action effects versus 96/96 for the registered alternative.; The comparison also checked 192 constructed null units; the result is bounded to tested one-step simulated game segments.
evidence.unknown: External generalization, independent replication and downstream real-world impact were not established by the reviewed source.
evidence.ai_role: Frozen pretrained DIAMOND models supplied frame predictions for the statistical tests

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
